transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-07 09:30 PT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Raj Singh (Silverpine - Head ML), Nina Lopez (Silverpine - CTO), Omar Reyes (Infra), Lily Chen (PM)

Auto-summary: quick econ recap, caching numbers improved tokens per dollar, discuss batching latency impact, security questions on KMS and private deploy.

00:00 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we have about 55 minutes, quick agenda - econ numbers from last week's run, caching + batching changes Ethan pushed, and then questions and next steps
00:22 Raj: thanks Maya, yeah we got the notebook you sent, skimmed it - overall numbers looked promising but we wanted to go deeper on p95 latency impact when you turn on prefix cache
00:35 Ethan: yeah so small context: last week we left cache off to get baseline tokens/sec. I flipped prefix/KV cache on for the mid-run and tightened batch window from 100ms to 40ms for a follow-up run, that gave us roughly +28% tokens/sec on avg and cost/op down about 21%
01:02 Nina: wait 28% is avg tokens/sec? what's the delta on tail latency, p95 or p99?
01:18 Ethan: p95 moved from 220ms up to 260ms in the 40ms batch window run, but p99 only had a small bump, like 420ms to 460ms. when we use slightly larger batch windows, p95 drops but tokens/sec also drops, so it's a classic tradeoff
01:45 Omar: can you remind me the base instance type and model? we need to correlate to our infra numbers
01:53 Ethan: yep, model is open-llm-7b-quant and instances were rtx-a6000-like equivalent, single-GPU per replica; we also tested a 2-replica continuous batching config for peak throughput
02:10 Raj: curious about cache hit rates - you said prefix cache on - what was hit percentage?
02:18 Ethan: hit rate varied by workload but averaged ~42% hit on the prefix cache across the dataset, some intents had higher, like 60-70%, others were low. important note: chat threads with repeated system prompts showed biggest wins
02:35 Lily: does that 42% directly translate to tokens saved? i.e., is it linear reduction in tokens generated?
02:42 Ethan: not 1:1 because KV cache reduces kv compute and some tokens still streamed; ballpark we saw a reduction in generated tokens by ~18%, but effective tokens/sec/$ improved more because of lower compute per token
03:05 Nina: okay, and batching - you said 40ms batch window, does that mean you're waiting up to 40ms to accumulate requests? how does that behave under our bursty traffic?
03:20 Ethan: yes, the window is a soft cap; under low qps we won't fill the batch and latency is close to single-request, under high qps we fill quickly and get better throughput. for bursty traffic we recommend adaptive batching policies which reduce max wait when queue length is low
03:40 Raj: did you try adaptive? we saw some spikes that made our UI feel sluggish last week
03:47 Ethan: we tested a rudimentary adaptive policy - lowered max wait to 20ms when QPS < 20, and that helped p95 for interactive flows. I'm planning a more sophisticated profile for the next run
04:05 Maya: quick question on cost math — you showed tokens/sec/$ in the sheet, can you walk through the assumptions? we need to make sure Silverpine's finance team will accept them
04:17 Ethan: sure - assumptions: instance hourly price (equivalent), sustained utilization at observed QPS, KV cache reduces effective compute by estimated factor from microbenchmarks, we also included network egress estimate and extra reserve for peak bursts. the sheet lists per-token compute cost, amortized infra, and added Redwood platform fee in a separate tab
04:40 Nina: are you including quantization gains? we run 4-bit q so inference kernels are faster
04:46 Ethan: yes quantization is included as a separate scenario - 4-bit yields roughly 15% lower compute time in our tests, we annotate it as model-quant scenario. caveat: some open models degrade quality slightly at extreme quant levels
05:05 Omar: on security, our security team wants to confirm: SOC2 in place? KMS integration for keys? SSO?
05:14 Maya: Redwood is SOC2 compliant, we have an enterprise sheet with SOC2 and ISO summary. KMS integrations are supported for Private deployments, and we support SAML SSO and RBAC controls. we'll attach the security pack after the call
05:35 Raj: perfect - for the pilot we might need a VPC peered private control plane, any gotchas?
05:42 Ethan: right now we support VPC peering and private deployments; main gotchas are NAT/eBPF egress rules and ensuring the right subnets for GPU nodes. Omar, if you share your peering CIDR we can run a checklist
05:58 Omar: I'll add that to action items - we have a standard peering template but need the exact ARNs you use
06:05 Maya: noted. back to economics - Raj, what are your target units? like tokens/sec/$ target to consider this pilot successful?
06:13 Raj: we want to improve our current provider by at least 2x tokens/sec/$ for the retrieval/assistant workflow. current baseline is about 45 tokens/sec/$ across our mixed workload
06:26 Ethan: our 40ms batch + caching run put us in the mid-80s tokens/sec/$ for similar workload in the synthetic test. real traffic will vary; that's why we asked for two weeks of traffic to simulate
06:40 Lily: and how do you account for prompt length variance? we have some prompts that are 1k tokens
06:47 Ethan: the benchmark bucketed by prompt length - longer prompts get proportionally more KV reuse so cache benefits compound for conversation flows. short prompts benefit more from batching efficiency
07:05 Nina: any concerns about fallback behavior? if cache misses or model variant fallback triggers, how do you keep latency predictable?
07:15 Ethan: Redwood supports policy-based routing - we can route by latency SLA and have automatic fallback to a smaller or cheaper variant; also graceful degradation returns truncated completions if we hit tail-latency thresholds. we log route metrics per request for auditing
07:35 Raj: competitors - we saw OtherCloud AI's pricing is lower at high volume but their p95 is worse; did you benchmark them?
07:44 Ethan: we ran a quick head-to-head; OtherCloud had slightly lower per-token price but they didn't have an equivalent prefix cache so our effective tokens/sec/$ still favored Redwood in our workload
07:58 Maya: ok let's capture concrete next steps. Ethan, you'll run a 24h throughput test with cache_on=true and batch_window=40ms and also an adaptive profile for interactive flows?
08:09 Ethan: yes, 24h test with both configs, will post CSV to the shared bench doc and include per-minute p95 and tokens/sec/$; also include cost sensitivity for quantization levels
08:25 Maya: I'll send the updated cost model and attach the SOC2/KMS notes and the peering template. Omar will provide peering CIDR and egress numbers
08:36 Omar: yeah I'll add that by end of day Monday
08:40 Raj: and we'll anonymize and upload two weeks sample traffic so you can simulate realistic distributions
08:46 Lily: last thing - can you demo canary routing and rollback? we want to see behavior if a variant degrades
08:52 Ethan: absolutely, propose a short live demo on Thu 2026-08-13, we'll show canary + A/B and automatic fallback to fallback-variant and how logs look
09:05 Maya: perfect. any other questions?
09:10 Nina: none from me
09:12 Raj: all good
09:14 Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and action items, talk soon

End of transcript
